_about: Rivalry events (Stage 6.4). They come in the week before a derby (derbyNext) or a game against a rival (rivalNext: a derby or a club with high heat). {rival} is that club and {owner} its owner, fixed when the event starts. Extra effects: heat (rivalry heat with that club), owner (how its owner feels about you, -1 to 1), claim (a public promise to win the match, judged afterwards like a press-conference promise).

events.title: {owner} has a go at {short}
events.text: A reporter reads you a quote from {owner}, owner of {rival}: "{short}? Lovely club. Like a museum. Nothing in it has moved for years." They want your reply for tomorrow's paper.

choices.label: Hit back hard
choices.hint: The fans will love it. The rivalry heats up.
choices.result: Your reply runs under the headline "Come and see what's moved".
choices.news: Owners trade blows before {rival} game|The {short} owner hit back at {owner}'s "museum" jibe. The build-up is now officially spicy.

choices.label: Laugh it off
choices.hint: Good for your standing with the press.
choices.result: "Museums are free on Sundays. Our tickets aren't." The room enjoys it.

choices.label: No comment
choices.hint: Nothing gained, nothing lost.
choices.result: The reporter sighs and writes "declined to comment".

events.title: {owner} proposes a bet
events.text: {owner}, owner of {rival}, drops by with a grin. "Friendly bet on the derby. The losing owner wears the winner's scarf at their next home game. Deal?"

choices.label: Shake on it
choices.hint: A public bet that you win. Win and the fans love it; lose and you wear their scarf.
choices.result: You shake on it. By the evening the whole city knows.
choices.news: Owners bet a scarf on the derby|{owner} and the {short} owner have shaken on it: the loser wears the winner's scarf. Somebody is going to look silly.

choices.label: Make it {amount} to a local charity instead
choices.hint: Costs {amount}. The press and {owner} will like it.
choices.result: {owner} matches it on the spot. The local hospice gets a good week.
choices.news: Derby rivals give to charity|{short} and {rival} owners will each give to a local hospice instead of a bet on the derby.

choices.label: Politely decline
choices.hint: {owner} will think you're no fun.
choices.result: "Suit yourself," says {owner}, and helps themself to a biscuit on the way out.

events.title: {rival} are sniffing around {player}
events.text: {player}'s agent closes the door. "{owner} at {rival} called me last night. Big wages, big promises. My client is happy here, but he'd like to feel wanted."

choices.label: Pay him a loyalty bonus of {amount}
choices.hint: Costs {amount}. He'll feel wanted.
choices.result: {first} is staying, and a little richer. {rival} will have to look elsewhere.

choices.label: Complain to the league about tapping up
choices.hint: The rivalry heats up and {owner} won't forget it.
choices.result: The league says it will "look into it". {owner} calls you a sore loser on the radio.
choices.news: {short} accuse {rival} of tapping up|The {short} owner has complained to the league after {rival} contacted {player}'s camp.

choices.label: Tell the agent you don't negotiate through rivals
choices.hint: Free, but {first} may feel a little taken for granted.
choices.result: The agent shrugs. "I'll pass that on."

events.title: Safety worries for the {rival} derby
events.text: A councillor and a police inspector want a word. The last time {rival} came to the {stadium}, there was trouble on the bridge. They want extra stewards, at {amount}.

choices.label: Pay for the stewards
choices.hint: Costs {amount}. Safe and sensible.
choices.result: Extra stewards are booked. The inspector looks relieved.

choices.label: Organise a joint fan walk with {rival}
choices.hint: Costs {half}. Cools things down; {owner} will appreciate it.
choices.result: Both sets of fans walk in together behind a brass band. Mostly in step.
choices.news: Derby fans to walk in together|{short} and {rival} supporters will march to the ground side by side behind a brass band.

choices.label: Leave it to the police
choices.hint: Free, but if it goes wrong, it's on you.
choices.result: The inspector writes something down and doesn't say what.

events.title: Someone painted over the mural
events.text: Overnight, the mural of {short} legends outside the ground was painted in {rival} colours. Their fans are celebrating online. The fans' group rep is furious, and the club shop has a lot of spare paint.

choices.label: Repaint it, bigger
choices.hint: Costs {amount}. The fans will be proud of it.
choices.result: The new mural is twice the size and has a better likeness of the 1994 captain.

choices.label: Paint a reply on the wall along their bus route
choices.hint: Costs {half}. Fans love it, the rivalry heats up, the press tut.
choices.result: The reply is cheeky and accurate. {owner} is not amused.
choices.news: Mural wars in {city}|{short} fans woke up to {rival} colours on their mural, and answered with a wall of their own.

choices.label: Invite both sets of fans to repaint it together
choices.hint: Free. Good press, and it cools things down.
choices.result: It takes all weekend and there is one argument about shades of blue. It looks great.

events.title: Everyone wants a derby ticket
events.text: {person}, from a local firm, wants 300 seats for the {rival} game to give to clients, and offers {amount}. Those seats would usually go to members.

choices.label: Sell the block for {amount}
choices.hint: Brings in {amount}. Members will grumble.
choices.result: {person} is delighted. The members' forum less so.

choices.label: Sell half, keep half for members
choices.hint: Brings in {half}. Nobody is thrilled; nobody is angry.
choices.result: A compromise. {person} says they'll take what they can get.

choices.label: Keep them for the members
choices.hint: No money, but the fans notice.
choices.result: The members' ballot is the busiest the club has ever seen.

events.title: {owner} invites you to dinner
events.text: {owner}, owner of {rival}, has sent a handwritten card: dinner at the best restaurant in town, "to talk football like adults". It is either a peace offering or a fishing trip.

choices.label: Go, and keep it friendly
choices.hint: {owner} will warm to you, which helps in future deals. The fans won't love the photos.
choices.result: Three courses and no arguments. {owner} insists on paying, loudly.

choices.label: Go, and talk business
choices.hint: {owner} will respect it; a little warmer.
choices.result: You talk transfers over dessert. Nothing is agreed, but the door is open.

choices.label: Send your regrets
choices.hint: The fans will like that you kept your distance.
choices.result: Your card says "busy". Everyone knows what it means.
